```{r setup, include = FALSE}
has_deps <- requireNamespace("phyloseq", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("vegan", quietly = TRUE)
has_plotly <- has_deps && requireNamespace("plotly", quietly = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 4.5,
  dpi = 120,
  eval = has_deps
)
```

This vignette walks through every **plotting** function in `micropubr`. Each
returns a `ggplot2` object you can extend with `+`, share a common set of
arguments (`group.by`, `palette`, `theme`, `plot.title`/`subtitle`/`caption`,
`interactive`, `return.data`, `verbose`) and forward extra `...` to their
primary geom. For the statistical, machine-learning and genomics functions see
`vignette("stats-ml-genomics", package = "micropubr")`.

> **Tip.** Pass `interactive = TRUE` to any plotting function to get a
> [`plotly`](https://plotly.com/r/) widget instead of a static figure — see the
> [Interactive figures](#interactive-figures) section below for live examples.

```{r load}
library(micropubr)
data(GlobalPatterns, package = "phyloseq")

# A lightly filtered subset keeps the examples fast.
gp <- phyloseq::prune_taxa(
  phyloseq::taxa_sums(GlobalPatterns) > 5, GlobalPatterns)
```

## Alpha diversity

`mp_alpha()` computes within-sample diversity and, given a grouping variable,
adds the appropriate test automatically. x-axis labels rotate on their own when
groups are many or long, so they never overlap.

```{r alpha}
mp_alpha(gp, measure = c("Shannon", "Observed"),
         group.by = "SampleType", test = "kruskal")
```

Switch the geometry with `plot.type` (`"box"`, `"violin"`, `"dot"`) or draw
rarefaction curves:

```{r alpha-violin}
mp_alpha(gp, measure = "Shannon", group.by = "SampleType",
         plot.type = "violin")
```

```{r alpha-rarefaction, fig.height = 4}
mp_alpha(gp, plot.type = "rarefaction", group.by = "SampleType")
```

## Beta diversity and ordination

`mp_ordination()` computes the distance, runs the ordination, draws group
ellipses and reports a PERMANOVA in the caption by default.

```{r ordination, fig.height = 5}
mp_ordination(gp, method = "PCoA", distance = "bray", group.by = "SampleType")
```

The compositional (Aitchison) PCA workflow is one argument away, and `envfit`
overlays metadata vectors:

```{r ordination-pca, fig.height = 5}
mp_ordination(gp, method = "PCA", group.by = "SampleType")
```

## Taxonomic composition

`mp_taxa()` shows the top taxa at any rank and collapses the rest into
"Other". It supports `"bar"`, `"area"`, `"heatmap"`, `"bubble"` and
`"treemap"` layouts.

```{r taxa, fig.height = 5}
mp_taxa(gp, tax.level = "Phylum", group.by = "SampleType", top.n = 8)
```

```{r taxa-heatmap, fig.height = 5}
mp_taxa(gp, tax.level = "Phylum", plot.type = "heatmap", top.n = 10)
```

## Differential abundance

`mp_diff()` visualises results from `DESeq2`, `ALDEx2`, `ANCOM-BC` or any
generic table. Here is a volcano plot from a generic data frame:

```{r diff, fig.height = 5}
set.seed(1)
res <- data.frame(
  feature = paste0("ASV", 1:200),
  log2FC  = rnorm(200, 0, 2),
  pvalue  = runif(200)^2
)
res$log2FC[1:20] <- rnorm(20, 4, 0.5) * sample(c(-1, 1), 20, TRUE)
res$pvalue[1:20] <- runif(20, 1e-9, 1e-4)
res$padj <- p.adjust(res$pvalue, "BH")

mp_diff(res, plot.type = "volcano", label.top = 8)
```

Other layouts include `"ma"`, `"forest"`, `"dot"` and `"concordance"` (to
compare two methods).

```{r diff-ma, fig.height = 4.5}
res$mean <- runif(200, 1, 500)
mp_diff(res, plot.type = "ma", label.top = 6)
```

## Phylogenetic trees

`mp_tree()` renders the tree with `ggtree`, optionally colouring tips by
taxonomy and drawing an abundance ring. (Requires `ggtree`/`ggtreeExtra`.)

```{r tree, fig.height = 6, eval = has_deps && requireNamespace("ggtree", quietly = TRUE)}
gp_phy <- phyloseq::tax_glom(gp, "Phylum")
mp_tree(gp_phy, layout = "circular", color.by = "Phylum",
        group.by = "SampleType")
```

## Co-occurrence networks

`mp_network()` builds a taxon co-occurrence network. (Requires `igraph`,
`ggraph` and `tidygraph`.)

```{r network, fig.height = 6, eval = has_deps && all(vapply(c("igraph", "ggraph", "tidygraph"), requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE))}
mp_network(phyloseq::tax_glom(gp, "Genus"), tax.level = "Genus",
           top.n = 40, node.color.by = "Phylum")
```

## Longitudinal dynamics

`mp_longitudinal()` shows community change over time. We build a small
synthetic time-series object to demonstrate it.

```{r longitudinal-data}
set.seed(1)
n_taxa <- 12; subjects <- paste0("S", 1:4); days <- c(0, 7, 14, 28)
samples <- expand.grid(Subject = subjects, Day = days)
samples$id <- paste(samples$Subject, samples$Day, sep = "_")
otu <- matrix(rpois(n_taxa * nrow(samples), 50), nrow = n_taxa,
              dimnames = list(paste0("ASV", 1:n_taxa), samples$id))
tax <- matrix(paste0("Genus", rep(1:n_taxa)), ncol = 1,
              dimnames = list(rownames(otu), "Genus"))
ps_long <- phyloseq::phyloseq(
  phyloseq::otu_table(otu, taxa_are_rows = TRUE),
  phyloseq::tax_table(tax),
  phyloseq::sample_data(data.frame(samples, row.names = samples$id)))
```

```{r longitudinal, fig.height = 4.5}
mp_longitudinal(ps_long, time.var = "Day", subject.var = "Subject",
                measure = "Shannon", group.by = NULL)
```

## Function / pathway abundance

`mp_function()` plots a feature-by-sample functional table (e.g. PICRUSt2 or
HUMAnN output) as a heatmap, bar or bubble chart.

```{r function, fig.height = 5}
set.seed(2)
fn <- matrix(rlnorm(20 * ncol(otu), 3), nrow = 20,
             dimnames = list(paste0("K", sprintf("%05d", 1:20)),
                             colnames(otu)))
mp_function(fn, plot.type = "heatmap", top.n = 15)
```

## Interactive figures

Every `mp_*()` plotting function takes `interactive = TRUE`, which returns a
[`plotly`](https://plotly.com/r/) widget instead of a static `ggplot`. The
figures below are **live**: hover for tooltips, drag to zoom, double-click to
reset, and click legend entries to toggle groups. This requires the `plotly`
package.

```{r interactive-alpha, eval = has_plotly, fig.height = 4.5}
mp_alpha(gp, measure = "Shannon", group.by = "SampleType",
         test = "kruskal", interactive = TRUE)
```

The same flag works for ordinations — hover a point to read off its sample and
coordinates:

```{r interactive-ordination, eval = has_plotly, fig.height = 5}
mp_ordination(gp, method = "PCoA", distance = "bray",
              group.by = "SampleType", interactive = TRUE)
```

...and for composition bars, where each segment reports its taxon and relative
abundance on hover:

```{r interactive-taxa, eval = has_plotly, fig.height = 5}
mp_taxa(gp, tax.level = "Phylum", group.by = "SampleType", top.n = 8,
        interactive = TRUE)
```

Multi-panel output (several measures, or `mp_combine()` figures) is assembled
into a single `plotly::subplot()`:

```{r interactive-multi, eval = has_plotly, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
mp_alpha(gp, measure = c("Shannon", "Observed"),
         group.by = "SampleType", interactive = TRUE)
```

Save any interactive figure as a self-contained HTML page with the same
`mp_export()` you use for static ones (just give it an `.html` name):

```{r interactive-export, eval = FALSE}
w <- mp_ordination(gp, group.by = "SampleType", interactive = TRUE)
mp_export(w, "ordination.html")
```

A couple of caveats worth knowing. Static-only annotations such as the
significance brackets drawn by `mp_alpha()` are not reproduced by the
conversion (the omnibus test still appears as the subtitle). And the circular
`mp_chord()` / `mp_circos()` figures are drawn with `circlize` rather than
`ggplot2`, so they have no interactive mode and ignore `interactive`.

## Theming and palettes

Every function accepts `theme` and `palette`. The defaults are colourblind
safe; swap them freely, or set them once with `mp_set_defaults()`.

```{r theme}
mp_taxa(gp, tax.level = "Phylum", top.n = 6,
        palette = "taxa20", theme = mp_theme_nature())
```

```{r palettes}
mp_palettes()
mp_palette("diverging", n = 7)
```

## Composing and exporting figures

Combine panels into a labelled multi-panel figure and export it at a journal
column width.

```{r combine, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4}
fig <- mp_combine(
  mp_alpha(gp, measure = "Shannon", group.by = "SampleType"),
  mp_ordination(gp, group.by = "SampleType", permanova = FALSE),
  ncol = 2, tag.levels = "A"
)
fig
```

```{r export, eval = FALSE}
mp_export(fig, "figure1.pdf", column = "double", dpi = 600)
```
